blocks.content: The continuous impact of breaking waves combined with rock fragments sculpts coastal landscapes through persistent marine erosion.

rows: Force of waves traps and compresses air in rock fissures, causing shattering.
Undercuts cliff bases and widens cracks.
Waves hurl sand, pebbles, and boulders against the cliff face.
Scours and polishes rock walls like sandpaper.
Rock particles carried by waves constantly collide with one another.
Reduces sharp boulders into smaller, smooth pebbles.
Weak acids in seawater dissolve soluble rock types like limestone and chalk.
Chemical breakdown and weakening of coastal rock.

items: Sequence of erosional landform evolution: Sea Cave -> Sea Arch -> Stack -> Stump.
Distinction between Abrasion (waves hurling debris against cliffs) and Attrition (debris colliding and breaking into smaller rounded pebbles).
Wave-cut platforms are formed at the base of retreating sea cliffs due to persistent undercutting.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Marine erosion is primarily carried out by the energetic action of sea waves, tides, coastal currents, and storm surges.
The four main processes of marine erosion are hydraulic action, abrasion (corrasion), attrition, and corrosion (solution).
Continuous wave impact at the base of coastal headlands weakens rock structures, generating distinct erosional features.
Evolution of coastal landforms typically follows a predictable sequence from sea caves to arches, stacks, and stumps.
